subject: Compiler directives
notes: §7.3.3 SR5 'A compiler directive is composed of the compiler directive indicator, optionally followed by the COBOL character space, followed by compiler-instruction. The compiler directive indicator shall be treated as though it were followed by a space if no space is specified after the indicator.' (cite.py --check 7.3.3 OK). TryParse skips optional spaces after '>>' and every stage consumes its word through that parse (PB794), so both spellings are one reading. Probes V1 (every 2023 directive written '>> WORD') and V2 (the same '>>WORD') both compile and run identically ('V1 W'/'V1 FREE', 'V2 W'/'V2 FREE'); F2 mixes '>> DEFINE', '>>   IF', '>>  END-IF', '>> TURN'. More than one space is also accepted, consistent with a space separator being one or more spaces. The golden pb794_directive_operands writes '>> SOURCE FORMAT IS FIXED' and the unit test asserts the no-space and space forms parse to the same operand. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the >> compiler-directive facility is absent from X3.23-1985; per-directive introducing editions are the §7.3.x rows' own, e.g. PUSH/POP added in 2023 per Annex E.3.3 item 38 and E.2 item 5)
